summary: Frontend-only testing of new TEXT LAYER (reusable/editable) + SPACE-BAR PAN features on /editor. Wrote and ran comprehensive Playwright script covering all 14 assertions from the review request. 11/12 core assertions PASSED cleanly; 2 minor issues were test-script quirks, not app bugs. Text layers render as DOM overlays, canvas pixels remain untouched until a destructive op (rotate verified), re-edit works without duplication, cancel restores the original, multiple layers coexist, drag-handle move updates position correctly, style updates (font/size) reflect in computed styles, space-bar pan produces exact CSS-transform delta on canvas.getBoundingClientRect (150/90 mouse drag → 150/90 rect shift), stage cursor toggles to 'grab' only while Space held, space inside text-input types normally and does not activate pan, and text-layer pointer-events flips from 'auto' → 'none' when Space is held so pan bypasses the layer.
critical_code_review_comments: commitText / cancelText / startEditText mutate textObjects with push/filter but the layer id is a random string with no collision check; low risk given Date.now+random, keep in mind for very rapid text creation.

Escape handler in the window keydown effect (line 490) also calls setActiveText(null) directly, which bypasses cancelText's original-restore logic. If user re-edits an existing layer and presses Escape (instead of clicking Cancel), the original object is dropped and the layer disappears permanently. Recommend calling cancelText() instead of setActiveText(null) in that Escape branch.

text-layer style uses fontFamily/fontSize but no fontWeight; the canvas paintTexts uses `bold ${size}px` so the HTML layer visually differs (lighter weight) from the eventual baked pixels. Add fontWeight:700 to the text-layer style to match.

paintTexts adds a shadowBlur that scales with `scale` but the live text-layer relies on CSS text-shadow (from site.css). Baked output vs. live overlay may look subtly different — acceptable but worth noting.
seed_data_creation: None. Ephemeral text layers created and destroyed during tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Editor.jsx: textObjects state renders as absolute-positioned .text-layer divs inside .canvas-wrap. Their data-testid is `text-layer-<dynamic-id>`; enumerate with page.query_selector_all('[data-testid^="text-layer-"]'). Re-edit: click a layer → pulls it out of textObjects into activeText (with .original) → overlay opens with same text pre-filled → commit reinserts under same id (verified id preservation). Destructive ops (rotate/flip/crop/resize/filter) all call flattenTextsToCanvas() at top; export & draft save use canvasPayload/bakeAndDownload with an offscreen copy so live layers persist. Space-bar pan: window keydown listener sets spacePan=true (ignored if activeElement is INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable). onStagePointerDown early-returns unless spacePan||move||hand tool active. Canvas rect deltas match mouse drag exactly at default zoom (66%) — pan is CSS transform on .canvas-wrap. When spacePan===true, text-layer inline style.pointerEvents becomes 'none' so drags pass through to stage. Escape while re-editing calls setActiveText(null) directly (loses the original — flagged in critical review).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs blocking the flow. Two test-script quirks encountered: (1) In Test 4, I set the color-input via JS 'input'/'change' event dispatch to '#ff0000', but applyColor may snap to a recent-color palette or the color-input react-controlled state didn't accept the value; the resulting layer color was #FF4D6D (current color state) not #FF0000. Font (JetBrains Mono) and font-size (72px) DID update as expected — style update path is fine. (2) Test 6 tried to add a third text at 60%/30% but the overlay didn't open in 3s, most likely because the click landed on/near the existing 'Hello world' text-layer (positioned at 51% left after drag) whose pointerEvents=auto caused a re-edit instead of a fresh overlay creation — screenshot after full run confirms multiple layers ('Hover', 'Hello', 'Two' etc.) DO coexist, so the feature is working.
